quest.title: Imaginary Maze of True Heroes
quest.description: Next to a mysterious Domain in Mondstadt, you and Paimon run into an old friend. She seems to be preparing some kind of special event...

talks.objective: Go to the garden in Mondstadt

dialogues.speaker: Souka
dialogues.text: After everything, I've finally made it to the place where the story of those two legends began. Seeing how much I've given to be here...

dialogues.speaker: Souka
dialogues.text: Surely fate will smile upon me too! It won't be long now before I'll meet them once more!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's that person rambling on about? Judging from how she's dressed, she doesn't seem to be from Mondstadt... D'you think she's from Inazuma?

dialogues.speaker: Souka
dialogues.text: Aha, you're here, and even sooner than expected! Time for a cheer to celebrate our reunion, "Twin Stars of Brilliant Valor"!

choices.text: It's been too long, old friend!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: S—Souka, is that you!? Paimon never would have expected to see you here in Mondstadt. What a pleasant surprise!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But weren't you previously helping Haniyyah prepare for the next tournament? How come you're in Mondstadt all by yourself?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And all those books in front of you... You're not here to recommend novels to passers-by, are you?

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: Ah, well, I suppose the main reason is...

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: I'm being hunted down by Yae Publishing House's editors.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hunted down!?

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: Don't worry, they're not literally going to kill me! They're just constantly pressing me to submit my work by whatever means necessary... I guess if you think about it, they're doing it for my own good!

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: As a once-popular light novelist, I had to keep producing new content non-stop, both to satisfy our readers' voracious appetites and to maintain my popularity.

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: But the speed at which our readers get through it all seems to know no limits! If I didn't keep up, it wouldn't be long before I found myself completely snowed under by new requests...

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: But I couldn't bring myself to rush through the story of my Fungi buddies just to get it finished. After all, it takes time to come up with a good idea and then gradually refine it.

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: If possible, I'd like to finish writing up the whole story, then go through the revision process before finally publishing it in its entirety. The last thing I want is to agree to serialize, and then have to rush to meet the deadlines for each issue.

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: So for now, I've decided to start working on a new main piece with a simpler, more manageable story instead. This way, at least the readers won't forget me!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Who'd have thought it... And to think, Paimon used to reckon light novelists had it easy!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A bit of sightseeing here, a bit of "field research" there, then... Poof! They write their novel in a fit of inspiration, the Mora starts rolling in, and it's time to start living the good life.

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: In reality, only the most naturally gifted writers work like that. For the rest of us, simply planning out and finding the inspiration for the next daily chapter is already enough to drive you to the edge of exhaustion.

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: Most people can only write so much before they start getting writer's block. And in all honesty, I'm no different... Why else would I have come all this way to Mondstadt with nothing more to go on than an old folk legend?

choices.text: So this folk legend's the key?

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: Spot on! And my plan is to use pictures and a broadcasting device to turn my novel into an audio-visual, three-dimensional reading experience!

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: The title of this all-new, avant-garde work of mine is "Labyrinth of Legend: A Hero's Journey."

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: A hero of extraordinary ability unknowingly enters a treacherous labyrinth devised by an evil sorcerer, where they must navigate their way past a whole series of complex mechanisms and deadly traps before finally unearthing the secrets that lie deep within...

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: But I haven't figured out how it's all going to go yet...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, you've certainly got Paimon's attention!

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: I'll have to think carefully about the core contradictions and rhythm of the story.

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: With serial novels, the key is to keep the reader on the edge of their seat, so the various puzzles that the hero encounters in the labyrinth will need to be the main story driver.

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: I just so happened to hear talk of a Domain in Mondstadt filled with all kinds of mysterious mechanisms, so I rushed over here as soon as I could, found it, and started my investigations...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're always so spontaneous, Souka! So... Did you find any inspiration for your puzzles in there?

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: There was certainly no shortage of inspiration, but I haven't managed to think of any ingenious solutions to the puzzles yet, without which the plot still feels pretty weak...

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: All it took was a regular trap to give me a complete battering, and now the clothes Ms. Haniyyah bought me are all ruined! Still, I came out with just enough intel to draft a few important sections.

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: When it comes down to it, I'm no hero, nor do I have any special abilities, so it's no wonder that I can't come up with specific solutions to the puzzles.

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: But for you two, the famous "Twin Stars of Brilliant Valor," that won't be a problem at all!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, this isn't a surprise, but it's not like we have godlike superpowers or anything, so what made you think of us?

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: Well, there's no way I could hire a whole team of talented individuals to come gather material for me. As such, I need an intermediary who's closely connected to all sorts of powerful individuals to help me explore the Domain.

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: #And you, {NICKNAME}, are the most experienced, well-connected, and popular person in all of Teyvat... that I can think of!

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: Simply follow the script I've provided and immerse yourself in a world of text, film, and your own imagination. And once you're in the zone...

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: ...I'm sure you'll be able to think of suitable heroes and work out how they'd overcome the perils of the labyrinth, based on whatever the situation before you calls for!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Imagining what happens based on text and images in a novel... We've never tried anything like this before. it's almost like we're becoming authors too!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If all the different people we know came to face this Domain, full of all kinds of mechanisms, there'd certainly be a high chance of lots of wacky stuff happening... Stuff that ordinary people wouldn't even think of!

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: And that's why you'd be perfect! This way, we can work together to finish designing my new book. On my end, I'll be sure to write a bestselling light novel!

response.speaker: Souka
response.text: And when that happens, I'll credit you as the co-writer, and we'll split the proceeds!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, you can always trust old friends to be generous.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright then, let's give it all we've got!

choices.text: I do seem like the right person, don't I...
I'm guessing it involves this book on the table?
Wait, uh... Who are you again?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You look so familiar... Is it really you, Souka?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, you might have forgotten, but Souka's a writer we met during the Fungi tournament. She's been helping us and Haniyyah take care of our Fungi buddies...
